---
title: A Node or Bun server
description: Deploy your bot to a VPS or a container by building one folder you copy over and start with node, or a single Bun binary without node_modules.
---

A host like a VPS, a container, or Railway runs one process for you. You give it a folder and one command that starts it, and that folder shouldn't carry your `src`, your dev dependencies, or the seedcord CLI.

`seedcord build` writes that folder. Point `build.start` at the file that starts your bot. [seedcord.config.ts](/build/config) covers `root`, `instance`, and the other keys.

```ts twoslash title="seedcord.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from 'seedcord';

export default defineConfig({
    root: './src',
    instance: './bot.ts',
    build: { start: './index.ts' }
});
```

```ts plain title="src/index.ts"
import seedcord from './bot';

await seedcord.start();
```

`index.ts` only starts the bot that `bot.ts` exports, and a bot from [`pnpm create seedcord`](/first-bot) already has both files. With `build.start` set, the build writes `dist/index.mjs`, which runs `index.ts`. Without `build.start`, the build writes a bot that other code imports, which [a package](/build/package) and [an embedded bot](/build/embed) both use.

## Building

<Shell run="build" />

```txt output
seedcord v0.21.5  build

  ✔︎ read config    197ms
  ✔︎ load bot       152ms
  ✔︎ type check     698ms  tsconfig.json
  ✔︎ bundle          36ms

  11 modules, 0 listed files, 8.7 kB → dist/index.mjs

  run      node dist/index.mjs
  compile  bun build --compile dist/index.mjs --outfile my-bot
```

Each `✔︎` line of the build output is one step. The three that do the work:

- **load bot** imports your `instance` file and constructs the bot, the same way `seedcord dev` does. An env value your config reads at construction has to exist in CI too, or the build stops here.
- **type check** runs `tsc --noEmit` against the `tsconfig.json` beside `seedcord.config.ts`, from your project's own `typescript`. [`build.tsconfig`](/build/config) points it at another file.
- **bundle** runs Vite and writes `dist`, with `index.mjs` as the entry, one `.js` file for each of your modules, and a source map beside each. The build doesn't minify the code. [Every code file under `root`](/build/config#keep-tool-files-outside-root) builds, whether or not your bot imports it. Always run `index.mjs` because it sets the paths that the `.js` files read.

The last two lines print the commands that start what it built. The `run` line uses the runtime the CLI ran on, so `bun --bun run build` prints `bun dist/index.mjs`. The `compile` line takes the binary's name from your `package.json`, without the scope. `@acme/my-bot` builds to `my-bot`.

### outDir gets emptied

Vite deletes everything in `outDir` before it writes, so a file from a source you deleted can't linger in `dist`. Before that happens, the build checks the folder. It continues if `outDir` doesn't exist, is empty, or holds an `index.mjs` that an earlier `seedcord build` wrote. Anything else stops it:

```txt output
[3117] build.outDir is dist, which already contains other files. seedcord build empties outDir before it writes. Point it at an empty folder, or delete what is in it.
```

That's `CliBuildOutDirNotEmpty`.

<Callout type="warning">

The check only reads `index.mjs`. Once the folder holds a seedcord build, Vite deletes everything else in it too, like a `Dockerfile` or a `.env` you put beside the build. Keep those outside `outDir`.

</Callout>

## Running it

The scaffold's start script runs the build with node's `--enable-source-maps` flag:

```sh
node --enable-source-maps dist/index.mjs
```

The printed `run` line doesn't include the flag, so add it yourself. Without it, a stack trace points at lines in `dist`. With it, node reads the source maps the build wrote and points at your `.ts` lines.

To run it on a host, copy the whole `dist` folder there, along with `package.json` and your production dependencies since `dist` imports packages like `@seedcord/gateway` from `node_modules`.

The bot's [web server](#the-web-server) listens on port 3000. To use another port, set `server.port` in `new Seedcord({ ... })`. [Reading a value](/build/env#reading-a-value) has a sample that takes it from a `PORT` variable.

If you copy only `dist` and `package.json` to your host, the bot looks for `.env` in a different place. [A built bot's .env files](/build/env#in-a-built-bot) has both cases.

## One file with Bun

`bun build --compile` turns the build into a single executable that includes the Bun runtime and every dependency inside it. The host then doesn't need node, Bun, or `node_modules`:

```sh
bun build --compile dist/index.mjs --outfile my-bot
./my-bot
```

Bun stores the bot's files inside the executable, under a virtual `/$bunfs` folder. The bot then never finds `seedcord.config.ts` on disk, even on the machine that built it, so it reads `.env` from the folder you start the binary in. Put a `.env` beside it, or set the variables on the host. The data files you list under [`files`](/build/data-files) are inside the binary already.

### Calling Bun's own APIs

`@seedcord/tsconfig` sets `"types": ["node"]`, which leaves `Bun.*` untyped. If your bot calls Bun's APIs, install `@types/bun` and add it to your tsconfig:

<Shell add="-D @types/bun" />

```json title="tsconfig.json"
{
    "extends": "@seedcord/tsconfig/node",
    "compilerOptions": {
        "types": ["node", "bun", "vite/client"]
    }
}
```

A bot that calls `Bun.*` only runs on Bun after that, so use these APIs only if you've already picked Bun for production.

## The web server

A bot on Node or Bun runs one web server. It answers your host's health check and any [plugin routes](/writing-plugins/web-requests), and on an http bot it's also where Discord posts interactions. The `server` key holds all of its settings:

```ts twoslash title="src/bot.ts"
import { Seedcord } from '@seedcord/gateway';
import { GatewayIntentBits } from 'discord.js';

export default new Seedcord({
    bot: {
        clientOptions: { intents: [GatewayIntentBits.Guilds] },
        interactions: { path: './handlers' },
        commands: { path: './commands' },
        events: { path: null }
    },
    subscribers: { path: null },
    server: {
        port: 8080,
        health: '/healthz',
        url: 'https://bot.example.com'
    }
});
```

This bot listens on port 8080 and answers its health check on `/healthz`. Every key is optional, and a gateway bot and an http bot take the same ones:

{/* prettier-ignore-start */}

| key | default | what it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `port` | `3000` | the port that the server listens on. `false` keeps the bot off every port, for a bot [inside your own server](/build/embed) |
| `host` | every network interface | the interface it listens on. Set it if the server should only listen inside a container network |
| `health` | `'/health'` | the path that answers the health check. `false` turns it off |
| `bodyLimit` | `1048576` | the largest request body the server reads, in bytes. A larger one gets a 413 before any plugin runs |
| `url` | none | [the address people reach your bot at](#your-bots-address) |

{/* prettier-ignore-end */}

<Callout type="transport" only="edge">

Cloudflare runs the server for a bot on Workers, so its `server` takes only `url`. A Workers bot doesn't answer a health path.

</Callout>

### The health check

Most hosting platforms call an http endpoint to check that your process is still alive. The health path answers 503 until every plugin's `ready()` has finished, then 200. Once shutdown starts, it answers 503 again. It answers the same way under `seedcord dev`.

Set `health` to another path if your host expects its health check somewhere else, or to `false` if your host doesn't call it. A gateway bot with `health: false` opens its server only if a plugin has [`fetch()`](ref:core/Plugin.fetch).

### Your bot's address

Some plugins have to tell another service where your bot is, like a webhook URL that you paste into GitHub. The bot can't work out its own public address because requests usually reach it through a proxy or your host's router. Set `server.url` to the address people reach it at, as the sample above does. If your host serves the bot under a path, include the path.

A plugin reads that address as [`core.url`](ref:core/CoreBase.url). If a plugin reads it and `server.url` isn't set, the bot throws:

```txt output
[1242] A plugin or your code read core.url, but server.url isn't set. Add server: { url: 'https://your-bot.example.com' } to the config you pass to new Seedcord(), with the address people reach your bot at.
```

You don't have to set `url` while you develop. Under `seedcord dev`, a bot without one uses its own localhost address, like `http://localhost:3000`. An http bot whose [`dev.tunnel`](/tooling/tunnel#when-you-already-have-a-url) is a URL uses that URL. A bot with `server: { port: false }` doesn't have a localhost address, so give it a `url`.

## When the build fails

The build prints the error under the step that failed. Problems in `seedcord.config.ts` itself, like an `outDir` that holds `root`, come first, all at once. [Config mistakes](/build/config#config-mistakes) lists them.

{/* prettier-ignore-start */}

| what happened | the error |
| --- | --- |
| a type error in your project | `CliBuildFailed`, with the compiler's output cut to its first 24,000 characters |
| no `tsconfig.json` beside the config, or `build.tsconfig` points at a missing file | `CliTsconfigNotFound` |
| the project doesn't install `typescript` | `CliDependencyMissing` |
| the `build.start` file doesn't exist | `CliFileNotFound`, with `build.start` in the message |
| `outDir` holds files from something else | `CliBuildOutDirNotEmpty` |
| your bot throws while it loads, like an env value it reads at construction is missing | `CoreImportFailed`, with your bot's own error after it |
| a Vite plugin or an import fails while bundling | `CliBundleFailed`, with Vite's reason |
| two files under `root` build to one name, like `a.ts` and `a.js` | `CliProblems`, listing a `CoreDuplicateName` for each pair |
| a file or folder in the project has a `#` in its path | `CliPathHasHash` |

{/* prettier-ignore-end */}

Run the build with `--verbose` to see the resolved config and the full stack of any seedcord error.
